Handoff from a PR-triage session. Four open PRs in entireio/cli, all by the external contributor `stale2000`, all filed 2026-06-09/10, all still open. Please investigate each one and give me a per-PR verdict: is the bug real on current origin/main, is the fix correct, and what should happen to the PR.

My triage already established the following against origin/main. Treat it as a starting point to verify, not as ground truth - I want you to check each claim yourself and tell me where I'm wrong.

## #1396 [bug] Restore native Windows interactive prompts
Files: cmd/entire/cli/interactive/{interactive.go,tty*.go}, login.go, strategy/manual_commit_hooks.go
What I found: `CanPromptInteractively()` (cmd/entire/cli/interactive/interactive.go, the /dev/tty open near line 55) has no `runtime.GOOS` branch anywhere. On Windows the `os.OpenFile("/dev/tty", ...)` fails, the function returns false, and every interactive prompt in the CLI is silently suppressed. `interactive/rawmode_other.go` states the assumption out loud: "Those platforms don't have a /dev/tty for CanPromptInteractively to open either, so this path is not reached in practice." I grepped for `GOOS == "windows"` across non-test, non-md files and found it only in agent/registry.go, testutil/testutil.go, e2e/agents/claude.go and internal/entireclient/userdirs/userdirs.go - none of them terminal detection. WINDOWS.md only records that interactive *tests* are skipped on Windows (line 70), which is consistent with nobody having noticed the product gap.
This PR has ZERO reviews. Highest priority of the four.
Worth determining: what does a Windows user actually lose today (which prompts), and does the PR's tty_windows.go approach match how the repo handles other platform splits.

## #1394 [bug] Preserve Claude subagent token totals during condensation
Files: cmd/entire/cli/strategy/manual_commit_condensation.go
What I found: main still passes `""` as the subagents dir at BOTH call sites - manual_commit_condensation.go:1471 and :1517 (`agent.CalculateTokenUsage(ctx, ag, data.Transcript, checkpointTranscriptStart, "")`). Those are exactly the two lines the PR changes. Notably the `//TODO: why do we not use here subagents dir?` marker that used to sit on those lines has since been DELETED from main without the behaviour changing, so the signpost is gone but the bug isn't.
The PR author himself flagged uncertainty in the description ("I noticed the log saying that the bug might be intentional? Or it is unknown why it is written this way?"). Please settle that question: is passing "" deliberate, and if so where is that recorded? Check whether the subagents dir path the PR constructs (`filepath.Join(filepath.Dir(transcriptPath), sessionID, "subagents")`) is right for each agent, not just Claude Code.

## #1408 [bug] Fix rewind of tracked checkpoint deletions
Files: cmd/entire/cli/strategy/manual_commit_rewind.go, rewind_test.go
What I found: neither `deleteTrackedFilesMissingFromCheckpoint` nor `trackedFilesInTree` exists on main, and main's `Rewind` still only deletes *untracked* files absent from the checkpoint - it ignores tracked files that the checkpoint doesn't contain. ZERO reviews.
The author wrote "I'm having a difficult time wrapping my head around this bug, but the logs pretty clearly keep insisting that there is an issue." So the diagnosis needs independent confirmation. Build the scenario and prove or disprove it: does `entire checkpoint rewind` leave behind a tracked file that the checkpoint says was deleted? Note the PR also swallows a context-cancellation error that main currently ignores via `//nolint:errcheck`, so check the error handling change on its own merits.

## #1391 [cleanup] Centralize form accessibility behavior
Files: strategy/manual_commit_reset.go, strategy/manual_commit_rewind.go, uiform/uiform_test.go, versioncheck/autoupdate.go
What I found: this one appears to have ALREADY LANDED by other means. `isAccessibleMode` and `WithAccessible` are gone from cmd/entire/cli/strategy/, and `huh.NewForm` is now called in exactly one non-test place: cmd/entire/cli/uiform/uiform.go:83. That is what the PR proposed. So I expect the verdict here is "close as already done" - please confirm, and check whether the PR's source-level guard test (the thing that keeps `huh.NewForm` centralized) exists on main in any form. If it doesn't, that guard is the one piece worth salvaging.
Side finding while I was there: CLAUDE.md lines ~1570-1591 still document the OLD pattern - it tells contributors to call `NewAccessibleForm()` instead of `huh.NewForm()`, and describes an `isAccessibleMode()` helper in the strategy package. Both are stale now. Since CLAUDE.md is the instruction file agents read, that section is actively pointing people at code that no longer exists. Please confirm and note it; it needs its own small fix.

## Constraints
- Do NOT post anything to GitHub - no PR comments, no reviews, no issue creation. Report back to me and I'll handle the posting.
- Do NOT push to any branch.
- Do NOT use `git stash` / `git stash pop` - the stash stack is shared across all worktrees on this machine and other sessions may be using it. Use a temporary WIP commit if you need to set work aside.
- Work only in your own worktree (/Users/soph/.herdr/worktrees/cli/soph-bugfixes-issues). Don't cd into other worktrees or the main checkout.
- Fetch the PR heads read-only if you need the diffs: `git fetch origin pull/<N>/head:pr<N>`.

## What I want back
For each of the four: (1) is the bug real on current main - yes/no, with file:line evidence; (2) is the PR's fix correct and complete, or does it need changes; (3) recommendation - merge as-is / needs rebase / needs rework / close as already fixed; (4) for anything you close or reject, the reference a human can cite.
Three of these four have never had a human look at them in three months, and the author is an outside contributor, so accuracy matters more than speed here.

@@ -0,0 +1,41 @@
+package interactive
+
+import (
+	"fmt"
+	"os"
+)
+
+// PromptTTY is a platform prompt terminal opened for both input and output.
+type PromptTTY struct {
+	in  *os.File
+	out *os.File
+}
+
+// Read reads prompt input.
+func (t *PromptTTY) Read(p []byte) (int, error) {
+	n, err := t.in.Read(p)
+	if err != nil {
+		return n, fmt.Errorf("read prompt terminal: %w", err)
+	}
+	return n, nil
+}
+
+// Write writes prompt output.
+func (t *PromptTTY) Write(p []byte) (int, error) {
+	n, err := t.out.Write(p)
+	if err != nil {
+		return n, fmt.Errorf("write prompt terminal: %w", err)
+	}
+	return n, nil
+}
+
+// Close closes the prompt terminal handles.
+func (t *PromptTTY) Close() error {
+	err := t.in.Close()
+	if t.out != t.in {
+		if outErr := t.out.Close(); err == nil {
+			err = outErr
+		}
+	}
+	return err
+}

+	in, err := os.OpenFile("CONIN$", os.O_RDONLY, 0)
+	if err != nil {
+		return nil, fmt.Errorf("open CONIN$: %w", err)

+	}
+	return &PromptTTY{in: in, out: out}, nil
+}

+

+	allowed := filepath.ToSlash(filepath.Join("cmd", "entire", "cli", "uiform", "uiform.go"))
+
+	err := filepath.WalkDir(cliDir, func(path string, entry os.DirEntry, walkErr error) error {
+		if walkErr != nil {
+			return walkErr
+		}
+		if entry.IsDir() || !strings.HasSuffix(path, ".go") || strings.HasSuffix(path, "_test.go") {
+			return nil
+		}
+
+		data, err := os.ReadFile(path)
+		if err != nil {
+			return err
+		}

+			return nil
+		}
+

+		if err != nil {
+			return err
+		}
+		if filepath.ToSlash(rel) != allowed {
+			t.Errorf("%s uses huh.NewForm directly; use uiform.New instead", rel)
+		}
+		return nil
+	})

+}
+
+func findRepoRoot(t *testing.T) string {
+	t.Helper()
+
+	dir, err := os.Getwd()

+		t.Fatalf("get working directory: %v", err)
+	}
+	for {

+		if parent == dir {

+	}

    36	func CanPromptInteractively() bool {
    37		if v := os.Getenv(EnvTestTTY); v != "" {

    51		if v := os.Getenv("CI"); v != "" && v != "false" {

     1	//go:build darwin || linux

     3	package interactive

    10	
    11	// ttyInRawMode reports whether the terminal behind f has canonical (line) input
    12	// disabled — i.e. a full-screen program owns the screen rather than a shell we
    13	// can prompt.
    14	//
    15	// Terminal-UI git clients (lazygit, gitui, tig, …) run git as a child process
    16	// while keeping the controlling terminal in raw mode for their own screen and
    17	// key handling. Such a child — including a git hook, and therefore `entire` —
    18	// still inherits that controlling terminal, so it can open /dev/tty
    19	// successfully. The /dev/tty probe alone therefore cannot tell a TUI apart from
    20	// a shell, and prompting there is broken in both directions: our output paints
    21	// over the TUI's screen, and our line read races the TUI's key reader for the
    22	// user's keystrokes, so the answer may never arrive and the git command appears
    23	// to hang (the reported symptom was lazygit freezing on the "Link this commit
    24	// to session context?" prompt).
    25	//
    26	// Canonical input mode (ICANON) is the signal that separates the two: a shell
    27	// restores the terminal to canonical mode before running a foreground command,
    28	// while a TUI holds it in raw mode for as long as it owns the screen. That is
    29	// also exactly the distinction the TUIs themselves draw — lazygit restores
    30	// cooked mode when it deliberately hands the terminal to a child (editor,
    31	// interactive rebase, custom subprocess commands), which is when prompting does
    32	// work and should happen.
    33	//
    34	// Checking the terminal mode rather than the hook's file descriptors is
    35	// deliberate: git's hook stdio plumbing varies by git version (stdin is
    36	// /dev/null, and stdout/stderr may be inherited or captured), so an isatty
    37	// check on those descriptors is not a stable signal, while terminal ownership
    38	// is.
    39	//
    40	// rawModeIoctl is the platform's termios read ioctl (rawmode_darwin.go,
    41	// rawmode_linux.go); rawmode_other.go covers platforms without termios.
    42	func ttyInRawMode(f *os.File) bool {
    43		termios, err := unix.IoctlGetTermios(int(f.Fd()), rawModeIoctl) //nolint:gosec // G115: uintptr->int is safe for fd
    44		if err != nil {
    45			// Can't tell — fail open so an unexpected ioctl failure never silently
    46			// disables prompting. This check may only ever suppress prompts we
    47			// positively know are unusable.
    48			return false
    49		}
    50		return termios.Lflag&unix.ICANON == 0
    51	}

    26	// form prompts respect the user's terminal palette and stay consistent with
    27	// the rest of the CLI's styling. Derived from huh.ThemeBase16 with a few
    28	// overrides — magenta selection (pointer + chosen options); titles and
    29	// unselected options use the terminal's default foreground so they invert
    30	// with the background (dark text on light, light text on dark) like the
    31	// checkbox bracket does.
    32	func Theme() huh.Theme {
    33		return huh.ThemeFunc(func(isDark bool) *huh.Styles {
    34			t := huh.ThemeBase16(isDark)
    35	
    36			accent := lipgloss.Color(palette.Accent)
    37			lightDark := lipgloss.LightDark(isDark)
    38	
    39			// Titles and unselected options drop their explicit color and inherit
    40			// the terminal's default text color, which already inverts with the
    41			// background. A pinned base16 slot (e.g. black "0") can't invert because
    42			// it always maps to that slot in both themes. Group.Title is copied from
    43			// Focused.Title inside ThemeBase16, and ThemeBase16 copies Focused into
    44			// Blurred wholesale, so clear the blurred variants too — otherwise
    45			// inactive fields in multi-field forms keep the pinned base16 color.
    46			t.Focused.Title = t.Focused.Title.UnsetForeground()
    47			t.Group.Title = t.Group.Title.UnsetForeground()
    48			t.Focused.UnselectedOption = t.Focused.UnselectedOption.UnsetForeground()
    49			t.Blurred.Title = t.Blurred.Title.UnsetForeground()
    50			t.Blurred.UnselectedOption = t.Blurred.UnselectedOption.UnsetForeground()
    51	
    52			// Magenta selection: the pointer (single + multi select) and the
    53			// chosen option(s), replacing ThemeBase16's yellow/green.
    54			t.Focused.SelectSelector = t.Focused.SelectSelector.Foreground(accent)
    55			t.Focused.MultiSelectSelector = t.Focused.MultiSelectSelector.Foreground(accent)
    56			t.Focused.SelectedOption = t.Focused.SelectedOption.Foreground(accent)
    57			t.Focused.SelectedPrefix = t.Focused.SelectedPrefix.Foreground(accent)
    58	
    59			// Blurred (inactive) button: no background chip and default text color,
    60			// so it reads as plain text that inverts with the terminal theme while

    62			// and blurred field variants (ThemeBase16 copies Focused into Blurred).

    99	// behavior and returns the user's answer. On user cancellation (Ctrl+C or
   100	// context.Canceled) returns (false, nil) so callers treat it as a "no";
   101	// on real form errors the error is returned wrapped.
   102	func PromptYN(ctx context.Context, question string, def bool) (bool, error) {
   103		answer := def
   104		form := New(huh.NewGroup(
   105			huh.NewConfirm().
   106				Title(question).
   107				Value(&answer),
   108		))

   112			}
   113			return false, fmt.Errorf("confirm form: %w", err)
   114		}
   115		return answer, nil
   116	}

Remove the restore half of the rewind machinery
The `rewind` commands were removed a while ago and nothing replaced them,
so the code that puts files back on disk from a checkpoint has had no
caller outside its own tests ever since. A whole-program VTA call graph
rooted at every cobra command constructor, every package initializer and
every main confirms it: Rewind, PreviewRewind, CanRewind and
checkCanRewindWithWarning each come back with zero reachable owners, while
GetRewindPoints, GetLogsOnlyRewindPoints and ResolveAgentForRewind next to
them still have real ones. CLAUDE.md has been calling this "machinery
pending removal" in so many words; this is the removal.

Gone from manual_commit_rewind.go: Rewind (the worktree overwrite),
resetShadowBranchToCheckpoint (only Rewind called it), CanRewind, and
PreviewRewind. Gone from strategy.go: RewindPreview, which only
PreviewRewind constructed. Gone from common.go: checkCanRewindWithWarning,
whose only caller was CanRewind, and with it countLines and
computeDiffStats, which nothing else in the package called. The last two
are in the same commit rather than a follow-up because leaving them behind
for one commit fails the `unused` linter, and a commit that does not pass
lint is worse than a slightly wider one. splitLines stays -- content_overlap.go
uses it. The countLines in cmd/entire/cli/explain.go is a separate function
and is untouched.

Deliberately kept, because they are live: GetRewindPoints and
GetLogsOnlyRewindPoints feed `entire checkpoint list --pending`;
RestoreLogsOnly and everything under it (restoredPromptPreview,
FirstDisplayPrompt, extractPromptsFromTranscriptBytes,
ResolveAgentForRewind, readSessionPrompt, classifySessionsForRestore,
ClassifyTimestamps, ResolveLatestCheckpointFromMap) feed `entire resume`
and `entire trail resume`. RestoreLogsOnly writes session logs, not
worktree files, so it is not part of what went. The RewindPoint,
RestoredSession and SessionRestoreStatus types and the "rewind point"
vocabulary are unchanged.

Tests for the removed behaviour go with it: the two PreviewRewind tests,
the three CanRewind tests, and the three Rewind execution tests including
TestShadowStrategy_Rewind_PreservesIgnoredFiles, which guarded the restore
path against reaching for go-git's Worktree.Reset. That hazard cannot be
hit by code that no longer exists; the go-git rule itself still stands in
CLAUDE.md for the paths that do checkout and reset.

refactor(checkpoint): use the existing token-summing primitive, and cap its depth
Review of the previous commit found the store-side half was reinventing
types.AddTokenUsage, which already sums the five scalars and recurses into
SubagentTokens, is already imported by persistent.go, and is already used in
production by agentimport. Two reviewers verified equivalence independently, one
by probing both against 7 shapes. Shipping as written would have taken the repo
from three hand-rolled TokenUsage adders to four, with the newest one being the
one whose own comment explained that a field-by-field copy is how the nested
total came to be dropped. aggregateTokenUsage, subagentTokensOf and their new
test are gone; the single caller now calls types.AddTokenUsage.

Propagating the nested total into the root summary turned out to introduce a
write-amplification vector, which the drop had been masking: token usage is read
back from per-session metadata.json blobs on the shared checkpoint branch, so the
chain depth is not trustworthy, and the root summary is re-marshalled with
indentation — O(depth²) in output size. A ~10k-deep chain (json's own nesting
limit) in a 200KB session blob measured out to a ~700MB root blob, written and
pushed. AddTokenUsage now truncates at MaxSubagentDepth = 16, matching the
existing reviewTokenMaxDepth convention. Real chains are depth 1.

Condensation side:

- The fill is now the else-branch of the whole-value fallback above it rather
  than a third sequential assignment. The two are mutually exclusive:
  accumulateTokenUsage already carries SubagentTokens, so the fill's guard always
  early-returned when that branch fired — it was dead work.
- Renamed to withSubagentTokensFrom and used for the identical copy-fill block
  inside applyBackfilledSessionTokenUsage (9 lines to 1). The abstraction was
  built and then not applied to the existing caller, leaving the load-bearing
  copy-not-mutate invariant documented in two places that could drift.
- Guards collapsed to one condition; doc comment cut from 26 lines to 15 by
  dropping bug history and a paragraph duplicated at the recompute site.

The live-path comment claimed subagentsDir="" for "the same reason" as the
shadow path. That was inverted: mid-turn the subagent transcripts are still on
disk, so the cleanup hazard cannot apply there — it is the one place the
documented gap could actually be closed. Both comments now say what is true, and
carry the measured ~29x cost that justifies the choice on both paths.

Tests: the new condensation tests folded into the file that already owns subagent
token invariants (renamed subagent_token_dedup_test.go -> subagent_tokens_test.go);
the second one was ~50 lines of arrangement duplicated from the existing
real-reset-path test wrapped around 6 unique assertions, so those assertions now
extend that test instead. The hand-rolled metadata-branch walker is replaced by
the store's own Read, which does not hard-code the sharded layout. A reviewer
disproved the copy-semantics assertions empirically — they pass against a
mutate-in-place implementation, because applyBackfilledSessionTokenUsage already
returns a copy on that path — so they are replaced by a direct unit test on the
pure function.

+// TestAccumulateTokenUsage_SubagentTokensReplacedNotSummed is a focused unit
+// test on accumulateTokenUsage: CalculateTotalTokenUsage (claudecode and
+// factoryaidroid) discovers subagent IDs from the full transcript and re-reads
+// each subagent transcript from line 0 on every call, so incoming.SubagentTokens
+// is always a cumulative-since-session-start snapshot, not a per-step delta.
+// Summing that snapshot across steps (as accumulateTokenUsage does for the
+// main-agent fields) would re-add a subagent's full usage on every subsequent
+// step after it was first discovered. accumulateTokenUsage must replace
+// SubagentTokens with the latest snapshot instead.
+func TestAccumulateTokenUsage_SubagentTokensReplacedNotSummed(t *testing.T) {
+	subagentSnapshot := &agent.TokenUsage{InputTokens: 500, OutputTokens: 250, APICallCount: 5}
+
+	step1 := &agent.TokenUsage{InputTokens: 100, OutputTokens: 50, APICallCount: 1, SubagentTokens: subagentSnapshot}
+	existing := accumulateTokenUsage(nil, step1)
+	require.NotNil(t, existing.SubagentTokens)
+	require.Equal(t, 500, existing.SubagentTokens.InputTokens)
+	require.Equal(t, 250, existing.SubagentTokens.OutputTokens)

+	// Second step within the same checkpoint window: the subagent transcript
+	// hasn't changed, so CalculateTotalTokenUsage returns the SAME cumulative
+	// snapshot again. Main-agent fields are per-step deltas and should sum;
+	// SubagentTokens must NOT double.
+	step2 := &agent.TokenUsage{InputTokens: 100, OutputTokens: 50, APICallCount: 1, SubagentTokens: subagentSnapshot}
+	existing = accumulateTokenUsage(existing, step2)

+	require.Equal(t, 100, existing.OutputTokens, "main-agent OutputTokens should sum across steps")
+	require.NotNil(t, existing.SubagentTokens)
+	require.Equal(t, 500, existing.SubagentTokens.InputTokens, "SubagentTokens must be replaced, not summed")
+	require.Equal(t, 250, existing.SubagentTokens.OutputTokens, "SubagentTokens must be replaced, not summed")

+package interactive
+
+import (
+	"fmt"
+	"os"
+)
+
+// PromptTTY is a platform prompt terminal opened for both input and output.
+type PromptTTY struct {
+	in  *os.File
+	out *os.File
+}
+
+// Read reads prompt input.
+func (t *PromptTTY) Read(p []byte) (int, error) {
+	n, err := t.in.Read(p)
+	if err != nil {
+		return n, fmt.Errorf("read prompt terminal: %w", err)
+	}
+	return n, nil
+}
+
+// Write writes prompt output.
+func (t *PromptTTY) Write(p []byte) (int, error) {
+	n, err := t.out.Write(p)
+	if err != nil {
+		return n, fmt.Errorf("write prompt terminal: %w", err)
+	}
+	return n, nil
+}
+
+// Close closes the prompt terminal handles.
+func (t *PromptTTY) Close() error {
+	err := t.in.Close()
+	if t.out != t.in {
+		if outErr := t.out.Close(); err == nil {
+			err = outErr
+		}
+	}
+	return err
+}

   533	func (s *ManualCommitStrategy) remapSessionForRewrite(ctx context.Context, repo *git.Repository, state *SessionState, rewrites []rewritePair) (bool, error) {
   534		if state == nil {
   535			return false, nil
   536		}
   537	
   538		newBaseCommit, baseChanged := remapRewriteSHA(state.BaseCommit, rewrites)
   539		newAttrBaseCommit, attrChanged := remapRewriteSHA(state.AttributionBaseCommit, rewrites)
   540		if !baseChanged && !attrChanged {
   541			return false, nil
   542		}
   543	
   544		hadShadowBranch := shadowBranchExistsForBaseCommit(repo, state.BaseCommit, state.WorktreeID)
   545		if baseChanged {
   546			changed, err := s.migrateShadowBranchToBaseCommit(ctx, repo, state, newBaseCommit)
   547			if err != nil {
   548				return false, fmt.Errorf("failed to migrate rewritten shadow branch: %w", err)
   549			}
   550			baseChanged = changed
   551		}
   552	
   553		// If a shadow branch existed, preserve AttributionBaseCommit so future
   554		// attribution still diffs against the original checkpoint base captured on
   555		// that branch. Without a shadow branch, keep attribution in sync with the
   556		// rewritten commit lineage.
   557		if attrChanged && !hadShadowBranch {
   558			state.AttributionBaseCommit = newAttrBaseCommit
   559		}
   560	
   561		return baseChanged || attrChanged, nil
   562	}

Committed checkpoints reported "subagent_tokens": null even for sessions that
ran many subagents — 0 of 30 sampled real checkpoints carried one. Two
independent drops:

1. Condensation recomputes token usage from the transcript with
   subagentsDir="", which by contract leaves SubagentTokens nil, and that
   recomputed value replaced what SaveStep had produced. The session-wide
   cumulative survived on state.TokenUsage (so `entire status` still showed
   subagent usage), but the value written to checkpoint metadata lost it.

2. The store's aggregateTokenUsage, which sums a checkpoint's sessions into the
   root metadata.json, copied only the five scalar fields — so even a
   per-session metadata carrying SubagentTokens produced a null total at the
   root.

For (1), fill from state.CheckpointTokenUsage.SubagentTokens: SaveStep already
rescoped it to this window (cumulative minus SubagentTokensBaseline), so
checkpoints stay summable instead of each re-reporting the session total, and
we avoid re-reading subagent transcripts that may already be cleaned up. The
fill copies rather than mutates — state.TokenUsage can alias that struct after
applyBackfilledSessionTokenUsage adopts it (Copilot CLI), and mutating would
overwrite the cumulative with a window delta, making resetCheckpointWindow
snapshot a too-small baseline. It also runs after that helper, which must see
the recomputed usage without the fill.

For (2), recurse into SubagentTokens. Summing is correct at that level: it
aggregates across the sessions of one checkpoint, and each session's value is
already checkpoint-scoped. (The replace-don't-add rule applies to accumulating
steps within a session, where each step re-reports a cumulative snapshot.)

Replaces the two `//TODO: why do we not use here subagents dir?` markers with
the actual reason. Known gap, now documented: a mid-turn commit that condenses
before any SaveStep in the window has no CheckpointTokenUsage to draw on and
still records no subagent tokens.

Investigated against `origin/main` at `c3a48a5d5`. No GitHub actions or working-tree changes were made.

## #1396 — Restore native Windows interactive prompts

### 1. Bug real on current main? **Yes**

`CanPromptInteractively` still unconditionally opens `/dev/tty`:

- `cmd/entire/cli/interactive/interactive.go:55`
- `cmd/entire/cli/interactive/rawmode_other.go:7-10` explicitly acknowledges Windows cannot reach the path.

Additional direct `/dev/tty` dependencies remain:

- Login key availability: `cmd/entire/cli/login.go:99`
- Login key reader: `cmd/entire/cli/login.go:872`
- Commit-link confirmation: `cmd/entire/cli/strategy/manual_commit_hooks.go:77`

Consequently, native Windows always takes the non-interactive branch unless `ENTIRE_TEST_TTY=1` is forced. Depending on the command, Windows users lose or bypass:

- Browser-first login and login URL key actions
- Session/resume and placement pickers
- Confirmation forms, including destructive-operation confirmation
- Interactive runner setup
- Commit-link confirmation—the hook auto-links instead at `manual_commit_hooks.go:485-487`
- Other gated doctor, trail, plugin, repo, setup, review, and investigation flows

### 2. PR fix correct and complete? **Correct direction, incomplete for current main**

Using `CONIN$` and `CONOUT$` is the appropriate native-console approach, and the platform split is consistent with the repository’s existing OS-specific files. I verified the PR branch compiles both natively and with `GOOS=windows GOARCH=amd64`.

However, it cannot be merged as currently written:

- It predates the raw-terminal protection added in `508c438e3` and changes `CanPromptInteractively` to return true merely after opening the terminal. A current fix must preserve `ttyInRawMode` on Unix.
- Login has since been substantially rewritten. The PR modifies the removed `waitForEnter` flow and does not fix the two current login `/dev/tty` call sites.
- Its `PromptTTY` abstraction does not directly fit the current login path, which passes an `*os.File` to Bubble Tea and `interactive.IsTerminalReader`.
- It has no runtime-focused Windows tests.

### 3. Recommendation: **Needs rework and rebase**

This is still a high-priority product bug, but not a merge-as-is or rebase-only change. Rework should centralize native console opening, preserve Unix raw-mode suppression, migrate all three current direct `/dev/tty` opens, and add platform-specific tests.

---

## #1394 — Preserve Claude subagent token totals during condensation

### 1. Bug real on current main? **Yes, but only in a narrower case**

The original general loss during ordinary post-`SaveStep` condensation has already been fixed:

- `manual_commit_condensation.go:564-570` restores the checkpoint-scoped value from `state.CheckpointTokenUsage`.
- `manual_commit_condensation.go:1129-1155` documents and implements `withSubagentTokensFrom`.
- Targeted current-main subagent accounting tests pass.

Passing `subagentsDir=""` is now deliberate, not an unexplained leftover:

- Shadow path rationale: `manual_commit_condensation.go:1464-1471`
- Live path rationale: `manual_commit_condensation.go:1513-1517`

There is still a documented gap:

- `manual_commit_condensation.go:1145-1148`: a mid-turn commit before any `SaveStep` has no `CheckpointTokenUsage`, so subagent tokens are omitted.

The PR’s test constructs exactly this no-`SaveStep` scenario.

### 2. PR fix correct and complete? **No**

The directory shape matches today’s centralized `paths.SubagentsDir` convention:

```text
<transcript directory>/<agent session ID>/subagents
```

It is consumed only by agents implementing `SubagentAwareExtractor`, currently principally Claude Code and the compatible Factory implementation.

But the accounting is wrong for repeated checkpoints:

- Subagent extraction returns a **cumulative-since-session-start** snapshot.
- The PR places that cumulative value directly into checkpoint metadata.
- After a prior checkpoint, it must instead subtract `SubagentTokensBaseline`; otherwise later checkpoints re-report earlier subagent usage and aggregate totals double-count it.
- The PR unnecessarily re-reads subagent files on the shadow path, despite the measured cost and the fact those files may already have been cleaned up.
- Its test only checks the first checkpoint, so it misses the double-counting case.

### 3. Recommendation: **Needs rework and rebase**

Limit the fix to the live, pre-`SaveStep` path; use `paths.SubagentsDir`; rescope the cumulative result against `SubagentTokensBaseline`; and test a second checkpoint/window.

Relevant already-landed work a reviewer can cite:

- `a5cf26df89b4a4f76597b216643941b254950e7f` — **fix(checkpoint): carry subagent tokens through to committed checkpoints**
- `80094e5037dc5032bd150955a815e3d85b0d74a8` — follow-up consolidating the correct accounting and documenting the remaining gap

---

## #1408 — Fix rewind of tracked checkpoint deletions

### 1. Bug real on current main? **No—the worktree rewind feature no longer exists**

Your starting point is stale here. Current main has no production `Rewind`, `PreviewRewind`, or `CanRewind`. `manual_commit_rewind.go` now retains only pending-checkpoint listing and logs-only restore behavior.

The old implementation did have the reported bug. I independently ran the PR’s regression scenario:

- Against the parent implementation, preview failed to include `delete-me.txt`.
- Against the PR, the test passed and the tracked file was removed.

So the historical diagnosis was valid, but there is no current command on which it can manifest.

### 2. PR fix correct and complete? **Historically sound, now obsolete**

For the removed implementation:

- Reconciling tracked HEAD paths absent from the checkpoint was the correct behavior.
- Propagating the `Tree.Files().ForEach` error was an improvement. The previous ignored error could allow cancellation to produce an incomplete tracked-file set and then continue restoration.
- Preview and execution were updated consistently.

The test itself would need modernization under current repository standards (`testutil.InitRepo` rather than direct `git.PlainInit`), but the entire tested production path has since been deleted.

### 3. Recommendation: **Close as obsolete/already removed**

Human-citable reference:

- `74e9f831070f19325bb88a7d994c3f3a814cbfe8` — **Remove the restore half of the rewind machinery**

That commit explicitly records that the rewind commands had already disappeared, the restore methods had no reachable production callers, and only logs-only restoration remains. `AGENTS.md:1388` documents the same current architecture.

---

## #1391 — Centralize form accessibility behavior

### 1. Bug real on current main? **No**

Current production form construction is centralized:

- The sole direct non-test `huh.NewForm` call is `cmd/entire/cli/uiform/uiform.go:83`.
- `uiform.New` applies both the shared theme and `ACCESSIBLE` handling.
- CLI-local `NewAccessibleForm` still exists at `cmd/entire/cli/utils.go:24-27` and delegates to `uiform.New`.

The old strategy `isAccessibleMode` helper is gone.

### 2. PR fix correct and complete? **Behavior already landed independently**

The behavior was implemented by:

- `b08f4ce6effaee6119855a368c5ace2b0c574d93` — **Route remaining huh forms through the base16 palette theme**

Unlike the PR, that commit correctly removed the now-unused strategy helper rather than retaining it with `//nolint:unused`.

The PR’s source-level guard test is **not present on main**. Its intent remains worthwhile: prevent future production code from calling `huh.NewForm` outside `uiform`. I would salvage that as a separate small change, preferably following the repository’s existing source-guard patterns.

### 3. Recommendation: **Close as already fixed**

Cite `b08f4ce6effaee6119855a368c5ace2b0c574d93`. Land the guard separately if desired.

### Documentation side finding

The documentation is only **partly** stale:

- `CLAUDE.md:1570-1585` remains valid for code in package `cli`, because `NewAccessibleForm` still exists and delegates correctly.
- `CLAUDE.md:1587-1601` is stale: it instructs strategy code to use the removed `isAccessibleMode` helper and direct `huh.NewForm`.
- `AGENTS.md` is a symlink to `CLAUDE.md`, so one edit fixes both.

That section should direct non-`cli` packages, including strategy, to `uiform.New`.

The contributor did essentially no follow-up work after opening them.

### Activity check

- **#1396:** One commit only. No reviews, comments, follow-up pushes, or visible Copilot feedback. Last meaningful activity was opening day, June 9.
- **#1394:** Force-pushed while preparing the PR, then left one self-review comment explaining their reasoning. No code changes afterward and no external/Copilot review.
- **#1408:** One commit only. No reviews, comments, follow-up pushes, or visible Copilot feedback.
- **#1391:** The branch received a merge from `main` on June 15, authored by Soph, followed by Soph’s request to remove `isAccessibleMode`. The contributor never responded or updated the code afterward.

## Suggested disposition

| PR | Action |
|---|---|
| **#1396** | **Take over and replace/update it.** Real, high-priority Windows bug. Start from current `main`; the old branch is too divergent and needs architectural rework, not conflict resolution. Credit/link the original PR. |
| **#1394** | **Maintainer follow-up for the remaining narrow gap.** Most of the reported bug landed independently in `a5cf26df8`; the existing PR’s accounting is wrong across checkpoint windows. Implement the documented pre-`SaveStep` gap correctly on current main, then close #1394 as superseded. |
| **#1408** | **Close, do not take over.** The affected rewind functionality was removed by `74e9f8310`. |
| **#1391** | **Close, do not take over.** The production behavior landed independently in `b08f4ce6e`. Separately add the source guard and correct the stale strategy accessibility instructions. |

I would not push thousands of current-main commits and major rewrites into the contributor’s old branches. For **#1396** and the remaining **#1394** gap, fresh maintainer branches/PRs are cleaner, with “Supersedes #…” and contributor credit where their work is reused. That also makes review history accurately reflect that the final implementation is materially different.
ok, 1408 and 1391 are closed. I'd also close 1394 then and do a new PR with a fix, would close then when this is in. do the same for 1396, can we do this one after another

Yes. I’ll handle them sequentially from current `origin/main`, starting with the higher-priority Windows prompt fix (#1396), then the narrower subagent-token gap (#1394). I’ll keep each as a separate local commit so they can become separate replacement PRs; I will not push or post to GitHub.

func TestCalculateLiveTranscriptTokenUsage_RescopesSubagentCumulativeTotal(t *testing.T) {
	t.Parallel()

	transcriptDir := t.TempDir()
	sessionID := "claude-session-123"
	subagentsDir := paths.SubagentsDir(transcriptDir, sessionID)
	require.NoError(t, os.MkdirAll(subagentsDir, 0o755))

	mainTranscript := []byte(`{"type":"assistant","uuid":"a-main","message":{"id":"msg_main","type":"message","role":"assistant","content":[{"type":"tool_use","id":"toolu_task1","name":"Task","input":{"description":"write helper","prompt":"write helper"}}],"usage":{"input_tokens":100,"output_tokens":10}}}
{"type":"user","uuid":"u-main","message":{"content":[{"type":"tool_result","tool_use_id":"toolu_task1","content":"agentId: sub1"}]}}
`)
	subagentPath := filepath.Join(subagentsDir, paths.AgentTranscriptFileName("sub1"))
	require.NoError(t, os.WriteFile(subagentPath, []byte(`{"type":"assistant","uuid":"a-sub","message":{"id":"msg_sub","type":"message","role":"assistant","content":[{"type":"text","text":"done"}],"usage":{"input_tokens":200,"output_tokens":20}}}
`), 0o644))

	state := &SessionState{SessionID: sessionID}
	usage := calculateLiveTranscriptTokenUsage(
		t.Context(), claudecode.NewClaudeCodeAgent(), mainTranscript, state, filepath.Join(transcriptDir, sessionID+".jsonl"))
	require.NotNil(t, usage)
	require.NotNil(t, usage.SubagentTokens)
	require.Equal(t, 200, usage.SubagentTokens.InputTokens)
	require.Equal(t, 20, usage.SubagentTokens.OutputTokens)

	state.SubagentTokensBaseline = usage.SubagentTokens
	require.NoError(t, os.WriteFile(subagentPath, []byte(`{"type":"assistant","uuid":"a-sub","message":{"id":"msg_sub","type":"message","role":"assistant","content":[{"type":"text","text":"done"}],"usage":{"input_tokens":260,"output_tokens":35}}}
`), 0o644))

	nextUsage := calculateLiveTranscriptTokenUsage(
		t.Context(), claudecode.NewClaudeCodeAgent(), mainTranscript, state, filepath.Join(transcriptDir, sessionID+".jsonl"))
	require.NotNil(t, nextUsage)
	require.NotNil(t, nextUsage.SubagentTokens)
	require.Equal(t, 60, nextUsage.SubagentTokens.InputTokens,
		"second checkpoint must not re-report the first checkpoint's subagent input")
	require.Equal(t, 15, nextUsage.SubagentTokens.OutputTokens,
		"second checkpoint must not re-report the first checkpoint's subagent output")
}

Shards are balanced by bytes rather than line count because transcripts mix short lines with occasional multi-MB tool results.
1419-  - The checkpoint metadata walk reuses the previous checkpoint's redacted blob as a prefix and redacts only appended lines (`checkpoint/redact_cache.go`), turning a per-Stop cost of O(whole transcript) into O(appended). The stored prefix must always end immediately after a `\n`, which is what makes plain byte concatenation reproduce the full result; content with a partial trailing line is therefore never cached. Eligibility is keyed on `paths.TranscriptFileName` (`full.jsonl`), **not** a `.jsonl` suffix — `transcript.jsonl` is regenerated in full each checkpoint and `full.jsonl.001` chunks are not appended, so neither should qualify. Reuse requires the prefix bytes to still hash the same and `redactionFingerprint()` (CLI version + commit + `redact.ConfigFingerprint()`) to match, so a rewritten transcript, changed custom rules, or a CLI upgrade all fall back to a full redaction. Bump `configFingerprintVersion` in `redact/fingerprint.go` whenever the regex layers change behaviour, or stale output can be reused. The cache lives in the git common dir, resolved without caching from the explicit worktree root through `gitrepo.ResolveWorktreeMetadata`, never under `.entire/`, because anything in the metadata directory would be walked into the checkpoint tree and committed. All three whole-transcript paths are covered: the shadow write walks files through `createRedactedBlobFromFile`, while condensation and the Stop finalize rewrite hold the transcript in memory and go through `checkpoint.RedactTranscriptCached`. Those paths do **not** redact the same bytes — the shadow write stores a sanitized transcript, condensation and finalize a sanitized *and* image-externalized one — and they stay separate simply because their keys are different strings: the walk uses its real tree path, the in-memory callers a synthetic key carrying the session ID (so concurrent sessions never share an entry). There is deliberately no scope enum; sharing a key would be safe (the prefix hash rejects a mismatch) but would miss on every checkpoint. The in-memory prefix is stored as a **file** in the cache dir, not a git blob: go-git deflates the whole payload before discovering the object exists (dotgit dedups the rename, not the compression), and above `agent.MaxChunkSize` the whole-transcript blob matches no chunk the store writes, so it would linger unreachable until `git gc` pruned it and silently reverted the cache to full redaction. `redactIncrementally` owns the whole-content fallback and takes the redactor as a parameter, so prefix and suffix cannot come from different pipelines; condensation and finalize share that pipeline by both routing through `redactSessionTranscript`. A per-subagent task transcript opts out with a nil repo: it is written once per task rather than appended across checkpoints.
1420-- Each committed session stores the (sanitized, redacted) transcript (`full.jsonl`, read by CLI resume/explain) plus a best-effort compact transcript (`transcript.jsonl`, generated via `transcript/compact`). Like `full.jsonl`, `transcript.jsonl` stores the **full compacted session** on every checkpoint (via `compact.FullWithBoundary`), so each checkpoint is self-contained and the session survives a mid-history checkpoint being lost/reverted/rebased. This checkpoint's slice begins at the session metadata's `compact_transcript_start` (a line offset in compact-output coordinates, distinct from `checkpoint_transcript_start` which indexes raw `full.jsonl` lines); a nil/absent marker means a legacy delta-only `transcript.jsonl` (read from line 0). The marker rounds toward inclusion when a streaming message straddles the boundary, so the slice never drops this checkpoint's content but may repeat ≤1 merged line at its head. Compact generation is best-effort and is skipped when the compacted output exceeds the 50MB blob cap (unlike `full.jsonl`, `transcript.jsonl` is not chunked — `full.jsonl` stays authoritative and the compact is regenerable); in the OPF finalize rewrite a failed/skipped regeneration drops the prior `transcript.jsonl` and clears the marker rather than shipping a stale, less-redacted compact. Both files are pushed with the v1 branch. The root `metadata.json` `sessions[].transcript` pointer keeps targeting `full.jsonl`; when the compact transcript was generated the session entry also carries a `compact_transcript` path pointing at `transcript.jsonl` (omitted otherwise) so external readers can locate it next to `full.jsonl`.
1421:- **Subagent task records** - subagent work (Claude Code's Task tool) is captured as durable `session.TaskRecord` entries on session state, a pointer mid-turn (declared transcript path + labels; background launches record at launch, completions attach files/tokens/path exactly-once via `strategy.CompleteTaskRecord`, Factory Droid Workers upsert). Condensation materializes each record — declared path first, agent-layout fallback, same sanitize → externalize → redact pipeline — into `tasks/<toolUseID>/{agent-<agentID>.jsonl, task.json}` inside the parent session's checkpoint (unavailable transcript → `task.json` with a stable path-free reason; the writer redacts `task.json`'s free-text `task_description` itself, since the record carries it verbatim); live records store transcript-so-far each condensation, completed records are removed after a successful write. `State.HasTaskContent()` is the trigger currency: records-only sessions condense, records never live on the shadow branch, and shadow-branch existence does not imply task content (shadow pinning keys on `StepCount` only). `SaveTaskStep` is incremental-only (post-todo).

The identity match is UNIONED with the worktree-matched set, never a replacement: a commit condenses every session with pending content in its worktree. Any session matched outside its home worktree is guest-linked — whether identity-matched or selected by the pre-existing single-worktree fallback — and is condensed and linked without mutating worktree-coupled state (`BaseCommit`, shadow-branch realignment) from the foreign worktree (`isSessionHomeWorktree`). Worktree matching is always computed (it is the sole mechanism for commits with no agent ancestry): imported sessions never link, and multi-worktree ambiguity is filtered to recently-interacting sessions (15 min) before declining. This deliberately turns some former ambiguity declines into a best-candidate link; `recentSessionWindow` is a correctness tradeoff because a session in a long-running build or tool call can age out and leave the other recent worktree to win. The stderr hint naming `entire session adopt` fires only from the commit-linking path, and only when identity matching could not rescue the commit either. ## Summary

- include subagent usage when a live mid-turn session is condensed before `SaveStep` has populated `CheckpointTokenUsage`
- derive the subagent directory through the shared `paths.SubagentsDir` layout
- subtract `SubagentTokensBaseline` from the cumulative extractor result so later checkpoints do not re-report earlier usage
- retain the existing cheaper state-based path for normal shadow-branch condensation

This supersedes #1394. The broader loss during normal condensation was already fixed by #1837-era accounting changes; this closes the remaining live pre-`SaveStep` gap documented in `withSubagentTokensFrom`. Thanks to @stale2000 for identifying and testing that live-session case.

## Testing

- `mise run check`
- `mise run lint` on the independent branch
- targeted strategy tests covering live cumulative rescoping, real condensation baseline capture, and multi-checkpoint subagent accounting
EOF

content.text:
Reviewed and addressed all findings.

### PR #2333

Fixed in `1ff38e4de`:

- Open `CONIN$` read-write so Bubble Tea can call `SetConsoleMode`.
- Added Windows raw-mode detection using `GetConsoleMode` and `ENABLE_LINE_INPUT`.
- Added a Windows regression test.
- Corrected the remaining `/dev/tty`-specific documentation.
- Replied to Cursor and Copilot comments.
- Marked trail finding `01M23A340N1ZVSRXQWEAYNMHVM` resolved.

GitHub CI is green except the old Entire Gates result has not refreshed since resolving the finding.

### PR #2334

Fixed in `ff030700b`:

- Preserve the fresh cumulative subagent total on `state.TokenUsage`, allowing reset to advance the baseline.
- Keep only the baseline-scoped delta in checkpoint metadata.
- Skip the expensive full transcript scan when no subagent directory exists.
- Expanded tests for the directory gate, backfill, baseline advancement, and next-window accounting.
- Replied to Cursor and Copilot comments.
- Trail currently has no findings.

CI is currently running. Lint and targeted race-enabled strategy tests pass. A local full check encountered two unrelated existing macOS `/var` versus `/private/var` symlink-path test failures.

- #1396 (Windows prompts) - flagged as highest priority. The /dev/tty open with no GOOS branch, the rawmode_other.go comment that states the broken assumption out loud, the four places GOOS == "windows" actually appears (none of them terminal detection), and WINDOWS.md:70. Asked it to determine which prompts a Windows user actually loses today.
- #1394 (subagent tokens) - the two live call sites at manual_commit_condensation.go:1471 and :1517, plus the deleted TODO. Asked it to settle the author's own open question about whether "" is deliberate, and to check the constructed subagents path against every agent rather than just Claude Code.

these two work items came out of user PRs, can we give credits in the PR body

## Summary

- open the controlling terminal through platform-specific devices (`/dev/tty` on Unix, `CONIN$`/`CONOUT$` on Windows)
- route interactive detection, login key actions, and commit-link confirmation through the shared abstraction
- preserve the Unix raw-terminal guard used to avoid prompting underneath full-screen TUIs

This supersedes #1396. Thanks to @stale2000 for identifying the native Windows gap and proposing the console-device approach.

## Testing

- `mise run check`
- `GOOS=windows GOARCH=amd64 go test -c ./cmd/entire/cli/interactive`
- `GOOS=windows GOARCH=amd64 go test -c ./cmd/entire/cli/strategy`
- `GOOS=windows GOARCH=amd64 go test -c ./cmd/entire/cli`

Native Windows terminal interaction was not manually tested.

<!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY -->

> [!NOTE]
> **Medium Risk**
> Changes when prompts appear and how login/hook TTY I/O works on Windows and all platforms that use the new abstraction; behavior on Unix is intended to be preserved but regressions in TUI detection or terminal cleanup would affect commit hooks and sign-in UX.
> 
> **Overview**
> **Restores interactive prompts on Windows** by opening the controlling console through **`CONIN$` / `CONOUT$`** instead of Unix-only **`/dev/tty`**, while keeping **`/dev/tty`** on Unix and failing closed on unsupported platforms.
> 
> Adds a shared **`PromptTTY`** wrapper with **`OpenPromptTTY()`** and routes **`CanPromptInteractively()`**, login keyboard actions (Bubble Tea), and commit-link **`askConfirmTTY`** through it. **Unix raw-mode detection** (skip prompts under full-screen TUIs) still runs on the input handle. **Docs** (`CLAUDE.md`) now describe the platform-specific terminal probe and **`CONIN$`/`CONOUT$`** as fixed paths outside **`os.Root`** confinement.

## Summary

A mid-turn commit that condenses before any `SaveStep` has run in the window has no `CheckpointTokenUsage` to draw the subagent total from, so the committed checkpoint recorded `"subagent_tokens": null` even though the subagent transcripts were still sitting on disk. This was the "known gap" documented on `withSubagentTokensFrom`; it closes it.

- `extractSessionDataFromLiveTranscript` now resolves the session's subagents directory (`paths.SubagentsDir`, the same layout `lifecycle.go`, `review/manifest.go`, and `agentimport` use) and passes it to `agent.CalculateTokenUsage`, so the live path counts subagents instead of always yielding nil.
- That extractor returns a cumulative-since-session-start total, so `calculateLiveTranscriptTokenUsage` rescopes it against `SubagentTokensBaseline` before it becomes checkpoint metadata — the same subtraction `SaveStep` already does, so later checkpoints report their own share rather than re-reporting the session total.
- The fresh cumulative snapshot is kept on `state.TokenUsage`, because that is what `resetCheckpointWindow` snapshots as the *next* window's baseline. `applyBackfilledSessionTokenUsage` therefore switches to `withCumulativeSubagentTokensFrom`: the old `withSubagentTokensFrom` only filled a *nil* nested value, so on this path it left the just-computed window delta on session state, the baseline regressed to the delta, and the following checkpoint re-reported the full cumulative.
- The full scan is gated on the subagents directory actually existing (`liveSubagentsDir`, resolved through the agent's own `SessionStore` so the path stays inside the session directory). Re-reading every subagent transcript costs roughly 29x the main-transcript-only call, so sessions with no subagents — the common case — keep the cheap path.
- Shadow-branch condensation is deliberately unchanged: it still fills from the already-rescoped `state.CheckpointTokenUsage`, and `withSubagentTokensFrom` keeps that job.
- `CLAUDE.md`'s token-usage-scoping paragraph now describes both paths instead of only the shadow one.

This supersedes #1394. The broader loss during normal condensation was already fixed by `a5cf26df8`; this closes the remaining live pre-`SaveStep` case. Thanks to @stale2000 for identifying and testing it.

## Testing

- `TestCalculateLiveTranscriptTokenUsage_RescopesSubagentCumulativeTotal` — drives two logical checkpoints over a real Claude Code transcript plus a subagent transcript: the first records the full 200, and after `RebaselineSubagentTokens` the second records only the 60 the subagent grew by, while session state advances to the 260 cumulative. It also asserts the backfill does not overwrite that cumulative with the checkpoint delta.
- `TestLiveSubagentsDir_OnlyEnablesFullScanWhenDirectoryExists` — pins the cost gate in both directions.
- The pre-existing `TestCondenseSessionByID_CapturesSubagentBaselineViaRealResetPath` and the `SaveStep` rescoping tests continue to cover the shadow-branch path end to end.
<!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY -->
---

> [!NOTE]
> **Medium Risk**
> Changes checkpoint token metadata for a specific condensation timing (live pre-SaveStep); incorrect baseline math could misreport subagent usage in checkpoints, but the pattern matches existing rescoping and is covered by new tests.
> 
> **Overview**
> **Live mid-turn condensation** (before `SaveStep` has filled `CheckpointTokenUsage`) now records **subagent token usage** in checkpoint metadata instead of omitting it.
> 
> The live transcript path calls new `calculateLiveTranscriptTokenUsage`, which resolves the subagent directory via `paths.SubagentsDir`, runs the same cumulative extractor as other live reads, then **subtracts `SubagentTokensBaseline`** so each checkpoint stores a delta rather than re-reporting prior subagent usage. Shadow-branch condensation still uses the cheaper `withSubagentTokensFrom` / `CheckpointTokenUsage` path.
> 
> Docs in `CLAUDE.md` describe this branch of token scoping; the old “known gap” comment on `withSubagentTokensFrom` is removed. Tests cover cumulative rescoping across two logical checkpoints.
>

- The fresh cumulative snapshot is kept on `state.TokenUsage`, because that is what `resetCheckpointWindow` snapshots as the *next* window's baseline. `applyBackfilledSessionTokenUsage` therefore switches to `withCumulativeSubagentTokensFrom`: the old `withSubagentTokensFrom` only filled a *nil* nested value, so on this path it left the just-computed window delta on session state, the baseline regressed to the delta, and the following checkpoint re-reported the full cumulative.
- The full scan is gated on the subagents directory actually existing (`liveSubagentsDir`, resolved through the agent's own `SessionStore` so the path stays inside the session directory). Re-reading every subagent transcript costs roughly 29x the main-transcript-only call, so sessions with no subagents — the common case — keep the cheap path.
- Shadow-branch condensation is deliberately unchanged: it still fills from the already-rescoped `state.CheckpointTokenUsage`, and `withSubagentTokensFrom` keeps that job.
- `CLAUDE.md`'s token-usage-scoping paragraph now describes both paths instead of only the shadow one.

This supersedes #1394. The broader loss during normal condensation was already fixed by `a5cf26df8`; this closes the remaining live pre-`SaveStep` case.

## Credit

This work originated in #1394 by Bryan Wade (@stale2000), who identified the missing subagent totals and contributed the original tests and fix. Thank you for the investigation and original contribution.

    fix(interactive): open CONOUT$ read-write
    
    On Windows a console handle needs GENERIC_READ to be recognised as one: Go classifies a handle as a console by whether GetConsoleMode succeeds on it, and GetConsoleMode documents the read requirement. A write-only CONOUT$ therefore took the plain-file write path, so prompt text bypassed WriteConsole's UTF-16 conversion and any non-ASCII character in it — askConfirmTTY prints the session's last prompt verbatim — was rendered in the console's code page. term.IsTerminal answers false on such a handle for the same reason, so a TUI library handed it would skip VT processing and emit escape sequences literally. This is the output-handle half of the access-rights fix already applied to CONIN$; charmbracelet/ultraviolet opens both read-write.
    
    Also rename the console-mode test so the real-Windows CI job, which selects with `go test -run '(Windows|MSYS)'`, actually runs it — it compiled there and was then filtered out. Stop wrapping PromptTTY.Read's error, so io.EOF stays comparable with == for io.Reader callers. Move the terminal-ownership doc onto readLoginURLActionFromTerminal, which owns the handles, rather than the test-only single-handle wrapper.

content.text:
Current state:

- **#2333 — Windows prompts:** merged into `main`; all checks passed and approved.
  - There is one clean, unpushed follow-up commit locally (`306444b05`) that opens `CONOUT$` read-write and improves Windows coverage. It is **not** in `main`.

- **#2334 — subagent tokens:** open and awaiting review.
  - Standard CI checks pass.
  - Entire Gates fails due to two open trail findings:
    1. Add entry-point coverage through `extractSessionDataFromLiveTranscript`, including a second checkpoint.
    2. Clarify/test `liveSubagentsDir` directory and symlink behavior.
  - The earlier Cursor and Copilot issues were addressed.

- **Working tree:** clean, currently on the Windows branch, one commit ahead of its remote.

Next steps are to land the Windows follow-up separately and address #2334’s two trail findings.

Here it is as one self-contained handoff.

---

## Review: trail #1275 / PR #2334 — `soph/fix-live-subagent-tokens`

**"fix(checkpoint): count subagents in live condensation"** — 2 commits, 3 files. Reviewed at extra-high effort with empirical probes against the branch; CI green on `ff030700b` except Entire Gates.

### Verdict

The fix is correct. The rescoping, the state persistence, and the failure/skip paths all hold up. The second commit's `withCumulativeSubagentTokensFrom` swap is a genuine fix rather than churn: `sessionStateBackfillTokenUsage` can return `checkpointUsage` verbatim (the `InputTokens > 0` branch and the Copilot fallback), and on the live path that value carries the scoped delta, so the old `withSubagentTokensFrom` would have made the next baseline the delta. Blast radius is limited to the live path — on the shadow path `checkpointUsage.SubagentTokens` is always nil at that point, so both helpers behave identically there.

### 1. Merge blocker (mechanical)

The branch is 4 commits behind main and missing `341c449b1` ("test: resolve temp dirs before comparing them against git-resolved paths"), which fixes the macOS `/var` vs `/private/var` symlink-hook test failures. Verified: `git merge-base --is-ancestor 341c449b1 <branch>` returns false. A rebase clears it. Trail finding `01M256PCN2YM` raised this and it was dismissed as "belongs in merge checks" — it's correct.

### 2. Highest-value code finding (not on the trail)

`types.SubtractTokenUsage` never returns nil for a non-nil first operand (`types/token_usage.go:75-90`), so `calculateLiveTranscriptTokenUsage` emits an all-zero `SubagentTokens` struct instead of nil when the delta is empty. Two consequences:

- `omitempty` on a pointer only omits nil, so checkpoint metadata gains a `"subagent_tokens":{all zeros}` object where the field used to be absent.
- Sharper: because `SubagentTokens` is now non-nil, `withSubagentTokensFrom` at `CondenseSession:570` short-circuits on `usage.SubagentTokens != nil`, discarding a genuine SaveStep-computed delta sitting in `state.CheckpointTokenUsage`.

Reachability of the second is contested — it needs `hasShadowBranch == false` with `StepCount > 0`, i.e. a stale `BaseCommit`, and `migrateShadowBranchIfNeeded` closes most of that window — so it may be narrow. The first is unconditional. Both are fixed by returning nil on an empty delta.

### 3. Best single suggestion

Replace the directory-existence gate with `state.CheckpointTokenUsage == nil || state.CheckpointTokenUsage.SubagentTokens == nil` — scan only when there is nothing to fill from, which is exactly the gap the PR set out to close. This fixes the cost problem and the refill short-circuit at once.

The existence gate as written stays true for the rest of a session after its first `Task` call, so every subsequent mid-turn commit pays the scan inside post-commit. The comment ~60 lines up (`extractSessionData`, around line 1464) measures that at *"~29x the cost of this call, enough to triple post-commit condensation for a subagent-heavy session"*. The new CLAUDE.md paragraph claims only the upside ("preserves the cheap main-transcript-only path") without naming the cost it accepts.

### 4. Three cheaper cleanups

- **Gate on `agent.AsSubagentAwareExtractor(ag)`.** `CalculateTokenUsage` only forwards `subagentsDir` for Claude Code, Factory Droid and external plugins; it drops it for Gemini, opencode, Cursor, Codex and Pi. One line removes the wasted store-open and lstat for most agents, and removes the nil-`SessionLocator` call at the same time — `ag` can be nil here, and `OpenSessionStoreAt` (unlike `OpenSessionStore`) doesn't nil-check. It's safe today only because `Name` and `Exists` never touch `store.agent`.
- **`withSubagentTokensFrom` and `withCumulativeSubagentTokensFrom`** have identical signatures and opposite override semantics, and are called with the state argument first in one site and second in the other. Swapping either pair compiles and produces a wrong baseline that only surfaces as token drift in a later checkpoint. Names encoding direction would remove the footgun.
- **`store.Exists` doesn't check `IsDir`**, so a regular file named `subagents` enables the expensive path and gets handed to plugin subprocesses as a directory.

### 5. On the two open trail findings

Both valid, both low-stakes.

`01M256NWZJ3F` (`liveSubagentsDir`) — I'd sharpen the framing. func TestLiveSubagentsDir_OnlyEnablesNeededSupportedDirectoryScan(t *testing.T) {
	t.Parallel()

	transcriptDir := t.TempDir()
	sessionID := "claude-session-123"
	transcriptPath := filepath.Join(transcriptDir, sessionID+".jsonl")
	ag := claudecode.NewClaudeCodeAgent()
	state := &SessionState{SessionID: sessionID}

	require.Empty(t, liveSubagentsDir(ag, state, transcriptPath))

	subagentsDir := paths.SubagentsDir(transcriptDir, sessionID)
	require.NoError(t, os.MkdirAll(filepath.Dir(subagentsDir), 0o755))
	require.NoError(t, os.WriteFile(subagentsDir, []byte("not a directory"), 0o644))
	require.Empty(t, liveSubagentsDir(ag, state, transcriptPath), "a regular file must not enable a directory scan")
	require.NoError(t, os.Remove(subagentsDir))
	require.NoError(t, os.Mkdir(subagentsDir, 0o755))
	require.Equal(t, subagentsDir, liveSubagentsDir(ag, state, transcriptPath))

	state.CheckpointTokenUsage = &agent.TokenUsage{SubagentTokens: &agent.TokenUsage{InputTokens: 1}}
	require.Empty(t, liveSubagentsDir(ag, state, transcriptPath), "an existing checkpoint total is cheaper and authoritative")
	state.CheckpointTokenUsage = nil
	state.SessionID = ""
	require.Empty(t, liveSubagentsDir(ag, state, transcriptPath), "an empty session ID must not collapse onto the parent subagents path")
	require.Empty(t, liveSubagentsDir(nil, &SessionState{SessionID: sessionID}, transcriptPath), "an unsupported agent must stay on the cheap path")
}

func TestExtractSessionDataFromLiveTranscript_IncludesScopedSubagentTokens(t *testing.T) {
	t.Parallel()

	transcriptDir := t.TempDir()
	sessionID := "claude-live-entry-point"
	transcriptPath := filepath.Join(transcriptDir, sessionID+".jsonl")
	mainTranscript := []byte(`{"type":"assistant","uuid":"a-main","message":{"id":"msg_main","type":"message","role":"assistant","content":[{"type":"tool_use","id":"toolu_task1","name":"Task","input":{"description":"write helper","prompt":"write helper"}}],"usage":{"input_tokens":100,"output_tokens":10}}}
{"type":"user","uuid":"u-main","message":{"content":[{"type":"tool_result","tool_use_id":"toolu_task1","content":"agentId: sub1"}]}}
`)
	require.NoError(t, os.WriteFile(transcriptPath, mainTranscript, 0o644))

	subagentsDir := paths.SubagentsDir(transcriptDir, sessionID)
	require.NoError(t, os.MkdirAll(subagentsDir, 0o755))
	subagentPath := filepath.Join(subagentsDir, paths.AgentTranscriptFileName("sub1"))
	writeSubagent := func(input, output int) {
		t.Helper()
		body := fmt.Sprintf(`{"type":"assistant","uuid":"a-sub","message":{"id":"msg_sub","type":"message","role":"assistant","content":[{"type":"text","text":"done"}],"usage":{"input_tokens":%d,"output_tokens":%d}}}
`, input, output)
		require.NoError(t, os.WriteFile(subagentPath, []byte(body), 0o644))
	}

	state := &SessionState{
		SessionID:     sessionID,
		AgentType:     agent.AgentTypeClaudeCode,
		TranscriptPath: transcriptPath,
	}
	s := &ManualCommitStrategy{}
	writeSubagent(200, 20)
	first, err := s.extractSessionDataFromLiveTranscript(t.Context(), state)
	require.NoError(t, err)
	require.NotNil(t, first.TokenUsage)
	require.NotNil(t, first.TokenUsage.SubagentTokens, "the production live extractor must wire in subagent usage")
	require.Equal(t, 200, first.TokenUsage.SubagentTokens.InputTokens)

	state.RebaselineSubagentTokens()
	state.CheckpointTranscriptStart = 1
	writeSubagent(260, 35)
	second, err := s.extractSessionDataFromLiveTranscript(t.Context(), state)
	require.NoError(t, err)
	require.NotNil(t, second.TokenUsage)
	require.NotNil(t, second.TokenUsage.SubagentTokens)
	require.Equal(t, 60, second.TokenUsage.SubagentTokens.InputTokens,
		"the entry point must subtract the prior cumulative baseline")
	require.Equal(t, 15, second.TokenUsage.SubagentTokens.OutputTokens)
}

- Each committed session stores the (sanitized, redacted) transcript (`full.jsonl`, read by CLI resume/explain) plus a best-effort compact transcript (`transcript.jsonl`, generated via `transcript/compact`). Like `full.jsonl`, `transcript.jsonl` stores the **full compacted session** on every checkpoint (via `compact.FullWithBoundary`), so each checkpoint is self-contained and the session survives a mid-history checkpoint being lost/reverted/rebased. This checkpoint's slice begins at the session metadata's `compact_transcript_start` (a line offset in compact-output coordinates, distinct from `checkpoint_transcript_start` which indexes raw `full.jsonl` lines); a nil/absent marker means a legacy delta-only `transcript.jsonl` (read from line 0). The marker rounds toward inclusion when a streaming message straddles the boundary, so the slice never drops this checkpoint's content but may repeat ≤1 merged line at its head. Compact generation is best-effort and is skipped when the compacted output exceeds the 50MB blob cap (unlike `full.jsonl`, `transcript.jsonl` is not chunked — `full.jsonl` stays authoritative and the compact is regenerable); in the OPF finalize rewrite a failed/skipped regeneration drops the prior `transcript.jsonl` and clears the marker rather than shipping a stale, less-redacted compact. Both files are pushed with the v1 branch. The root `metadata.json` `sessions[].transcript` pointer keeps targeting `full.jsonl`; when the compact transcript was generated the session entry also carries a `compact_transcript` path pointing at `transcript.jsonl` (omitted otherwise) so external readers can locate it next to `full.jsonl`.
- **Subagent task records** - subagent work (Claude Code's Task tool) is captured as durable `session.TaskRecord` entries on session state, a pointer mid-turn (declared transcript path + labels; background launches record at launch, completions attach files/tokens/path exactly-once via `strategy.CompleteTaskRecord`, Factory Droid Workers upsert). Condensation materializes each record — declared path first, agent-layout fallback, same sanitize → externalize → redact pipeline — into `tasks/<toolUseID>/{agent-<agentID>.jsonl, task.json}` inside the parent session's checkpoint (unavailable transcript → `task.json` with a stable path-free reason; the writer redacts `task.json`'s free-text `task_description` itself, since the record carries it verbatim); live records store transcript-so-far each condensation, completed records are removed after a successful write. `State.HasTaskContent()` is the trigger currency: records-only sessions condense, records never live on the shadow branch, and shadow-branch existence does not imply task content (shadow pinning keys on `StepCount` only). `SaveTaskStep` is incremental-only (post-todo).
- Uses the `post-rewrite` Git hook to keep local session linkage aligned after amend/rebase rewrites
- Builds git trees in-memory using go-git plumbing APIs
- **Location-independent transcript resolution** - transcript paths are always computed dynamically from the current repo location (via `agent.GetSessionDir` + `agent.ResolveSessionFile`), never stored in checkpoint metadata. This ensures log restore (`RestoreLogsOnly`) works after repo relocation or across machines.
- **Token usage scoping** - `SessionState.TokenUsage` is the session-wide total used by `entire status`; `SessionState.CheckpointTokenUsage` is the pending checkpoint delta since the last condensation. Checkpoint metadata must stay scoped to `CheckpointTranscriptStart` or the pending checkpoint delta. Cursor tokens come only from stop-hook payloads, while Copilot CLI can also backfill full-session totals from `session.shutdown`. Shadow-branch condensation's transcript recompute runs with `subagentsDir=""` and so drops `SubagentTokens`; `withSubagentTokensFrom` refills it from the already-rescoped `state.CheckpointTokenUsage`. A live mid-turn condensation before any `SaveStep` instead reads the still-available subagent transcripts when their directory exists, subtracts `SubagentTokensBaseline` for checkpoint metadata, and keeps the cumulative snapshot on `state.TokenUsage` so the reset advances the next baseline. The directory-existence gate preserves the cheap main-transcript-only path for sessions with no subagents. The store sums those scoped values across a checkpoint's sessions via `types.AddTokenUsage` (the single token-summing primitive — do not hand-roll another; a field-by-field copy is how the nested total came to be dropped in the first place).
- Tracks session state in `.git/entire-sessions/` (shared across worktrees)
- **Commit-to-session linking is identity-first** (`strategy/session_identity.go`): identity comes from `SessionState.Owner`, the `proclive.Identity` that `captureSessionOwner` already records on every turn start (first non-transient ancestor — proclive skips shells, `entire` itself, and the Go toolchain, so a human commit typed in the same terminal never matches). Commit hooks snapshot their own ancestry once (`proclive.CurrentAncestry`) and match every candidate against it in memory (`Ancestry.Depth`) — one hostname/boot-id/proc walk per commit, not one per session state — linking the commit to the session whose agent process is an ancestor — in any worktree (nearest ancestor wins, so a nested agent beats the outer agent that spawned it, and only a tie at equal depth falls to the latest interaction; host/boot/start-time guards defeat PID reuse and cross-machine matches; Windows cannot introspect and falls back to worktree matching). The identity match is UNIONED with the worktree-matched set, never a replacement: a commit condenses every session with pending content in its worktree. Any session matched outside its home worktree is guest-linked — whether identity-matched or selected by the pre-existing single-worktree fallback — and is condensed and linked without mutating worktree-coupled state (`BaseCommit`, shadow-branch realignment) from the foreign worktree (`isSessionHomeWorktree`). Worktree matching is always computed (it is the sole mechanism for commits with no agent ancestry): imported sessions never link, and multi-worktree ambiguity is filtered to recently-interacting sessions (15 min) before declining. This deliberately turns some former ambiguity declines into a best-candidate link; `recentSessionWindow` is a correctness tradeoff because a session in a long-running build or tool call can age out and leave the other recent worktree to win. The stderr hint naming `entire session adopt` fires only from the commit-linking path, and only when identity matching could not rescue the commit either. Under `go test`, `session.NewStateStore` and `NewStateStoreForWorktree` refuse to open outside the temp root so non-isolated tests fail loudly instead of leaking fixture sessions into a real repo.
- **Reclaiming sessions whose agent vanished** - not every agent fires a session-end hook, and any agent can be killed before its hook runs, so a session can be left un-finalized forever. `SessionState.Owner` — the same fingerprint commit linking matches above — is captured at every turn start by `captureSessionOwner`, and `State.OwnerExited()` reports it gone via `proclive.Check`. `finalizeExitedSessions` sweeps those inside `entire status` (text and `--json`) and `entire doctor`, ending them exactly as a clean stop would. **`OwnerExited` deliberately covers IDLE as well as ACTIVE** — an agent that finishes its last turn and then quits leaves IDLE, so gating on ACTIVE alone missed the common case; only already-finalized sessions are excluded, per the shared `State.IsEnded()` predicate. Liveness is Unknown on Windows and for cross-host state, where behaviour degrades to the `StuckActiveThreshold` timeout. Because the sweep runs inside interactive commands, its eager condensing is capped by `sweepCondenseBudget` across the whole sweep: every candidate is always marked ENDED (a single atomic rename — that is what un-sticks it from `entire status`), while condensing runs only while the budget lasts, so a multi-day backlog drains over successive invocations instead of stalling one. Skipping a condense is the existing fail-open path — PostCommit retries, and `doctor` reports the session as "ended with uncondensed checkpoint data".
- **Session-end hooks that run under a host deadline** - an agent whose session-end hook fires inside its own shutdown may be killed part-way through. Such agents declare `agent.SessionEndBudgeter` (Codex: 3s cap, process tree killed on expiry). The budget bounds **only** the eager condense in `endSessionNow`, so the cheap step that un-sticks the session is never the one given up on; it is set below the host cap with enough headroom for the shell wrapper and binary load, which happen before Entire's own clock starts. Unbounded is not the same as guaranteed, though: mark-ended runs under `MutateSessionState`, whose flock acquire blocks, so a concurrent condense holding the lock can push it past the cap and get the tree killed — the exited-owner sweep above is the backstop. The bound is best-effort (condensation doesn't poll ctx between stages), and being cut off costs duplication rather than data: an incomplete condense leaves `FullyCondensed` false and PostCommit retries, except in the window between the v1 checkpoint write and the state save, where the checkpoint is already committed and PostCommit mints a second one over the same transcript range.
- **Shadow branch migration** - if user does stash/pull/rebase (HEAD changes without commit), shadow branch is automatically moved to new base commit
- **Orphaned branch cleanup** - if a shadow branch exists without a corresponding session state file, it is automatically reset when a new session starts

## Summary

A mid-turn commit that condenses before any `SaveStep` has run in the window has no `CheckpointTokenUsage` to draw the subagent total from, so the committed checkpoint recorded `"subagent_tokens": null` even though the subagent transcripts were still sitting on disk. This was the "known gap" documented on `withSubagentTokensFrom`; it closes it.

- `extractSessionDataFromLiveTranscript` now resolves the session's subagents directory (`paths.SubagentsDir`, the same layout `lifecycle.go`, `review/manifest.go`, and `agentimport` use) and passes it to `agent.CalculateTokenUsage`, so the live path counts subagents instead of always yielding nil.
- That extractor returns a cumulative-since-session-start total, so `calculateLiveTranscriptTokenUsage` rescopes it against `SubagentTokensBaseline` before it becomes checkpoint metadata — the same subtraction `SaveStep` already does, so later checkpoints report their own share rather than re-reporting the session total.
- The fresh cumulative snapshot is kept on `state.TokenUsage`, because that is what `resetCheckpointWindow` snapshots as the *next* window's baseline. `applyBackfilledSessionTokenUsage` therefore switches to `withCumulativeSubagentTokensFrom`: the old `withSubagentTokensFrom` only filled a *nil* nested value, so on this path it left the just-computed window delta on session state, the baseline regressed to the delta, and the following checkpoint re-reported the full cumulative.
- The full scan is gated on the subagents directory actually existing (`liveSubagentsDir`, resolved through the agent's own `SessionStore` so the path stays inside the session directory). Re-reading every subagent transcript costs roughly 29x the main-transcript-only call, so sessions with no subagents — the common case — keep the cheap path.
- Shadow-branch condensation is deliberately unchanged: it still fills from the already-rescoped `state.CheckpointTokenUsage`, and `withSubagentTokensFrom` keeps that job.
- `CLAUDE.md`'s token-usage-scoping paragraph now describes both paths instead of only the shadow one.

This supersedes #1394. The broader loss during normal condensation was already fixed by `a5cf26df8`; this closes the remaining live pre-`SaveStep` case.

## Credit

This work originated in #1394 by Bryan Wade (@stale2000), who identified the missing subagent totals and contributed the original tests and fix. Thank you for the investigation and original contribution.

## Testing

- `TestCalculateLiveTranscriptTokenUsage_RescopesSubagentCumulativeTotal` — drives two logical checkpoints over a real Claude Code transcript plus a subagent transcript: the first records the full 200, and after `RebaselineSubagentTokens` the second records only the 60 the subagent grew by, while session state advances to the 260 cumulative. It also asserts the backfill does not overwrite that cumulative with the checkpoint delta.
- `TestLiveSubagentsDir_OnlyEnablesFullScanWhenDirectoryExists` — pins the cost gate in both directions.
